n1.text: You don't remember deciding to sit down on the office floor. You just are there, suddenly, and the room is very far away.

n2.text: The doctor says 'exhaustion' the way a mechanic says 'engine.' Three weeks of mandatory rest. Lighthouse launches without you.

n3.text: ✖ ENDING: 'Burnout.' Energy is a meter for a reason. Next time, drink the coffee, take the lunch, sit on the rooftop.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. Conversations stop when you walk up to them. Your invitation, you notice, came last.

n2.text: You did the work. Nobody wanted to do it with you. On Monday, HR suggests 'a fresh start in another department.'

n3.text: ✖ ENDING: 'Pariah.' Reputation is how the building feels about you when you're not in the room.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. Vaughn gives the launch speech. He thanks 'the team' and names none of you. Then he names himself, twice.

n2.text: The restructure memo lands on Monday. Your role is 'realigned.' Vaughn smiles at you in the lift like a cat at a bird feeder.

n3.text: ✖ ENDING: 'Outplayed.' Somebody had to stand up to Vaughn. Nobody did.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. You're on the stage for the launch toast. Someone you love is in the front row. Half the floor cheers your name.

n2.text: Nobody gets it all. But tonight, for one evening, it looks very much like you did.

n3.text: ★ ULTIMATE ENDING: 'Have It All.' Career, reputation and love, all at once. Rare. Earned.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. Your name is on the new org chart, one line higher than it was in Week 1.

n2.text: You go home alone, a little tired, very proud, with a better title and a heavier inbox.

n3.text: ▲ CAREER ENDING: 'Promotion.' The work paid off.

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. Lighthouse launches. You clap with everyone else. It was a good quarter. Not a remarkable one.

n2.text: Walking home, you think about all the people you meant to get to know better. There's always next quarter.

n3.text: ○ ENDING: 'On Your Own.' Life in the middle of the org chart. Try another route?

n1.text: Week 12. The Gala. You are not on the stage tonight, and you are not hiding at the back either. You are somewhere better: in the middle of the room, where people come to find you.

n2.text: Marcus mentions your name in his speech. Two people from other teams ask what you're working on next. Your inbox has an invitation to the planning meeting for the next big project.

n3.text: ▲ CAREER ENDING: 'A Seat at the Table.' You did good work and kept your life. Not the corner office, but a voice in the room that matters.
